name: Ohalo II wild-grain gathering and grinding
description: People gathered wild grasses and cereals and processed plant foods using ground stone.

impact.note: One camp's people gathered and ground wild cereals; a new food ability, on the long line toward later cereal use in the Levant.

date.label: About 23,000 calibrated years BP
date.basis: Source date for the documented context; BP conversion uses 1950 as reference where applicable.

events.statement: People gathered wild grasses and cereals and processed plant foods using ground stone.

evidence.supports: Ohalo II, about 23,000 calibrated years BP, yielded more than 90,000 plant remains. The authors interpret the assemblage as evidence for gathered wild grasses and cereals; grains cluster around a grinding stone.

Use-wear and residue analysis of the Ohalo II slab support grinding or pounding non-oily plant materials. The authors consider the evidence for intensive or routine flour production weak and interpret flour production as possibly sporadic.

events.caveats: Archaeological interpretation; cultivation, dietary proportion and continuity are unsettled. The grinding use-wear may indicate occasional rather than intensive flour production.

links.statement: Did cutting near-ripe cereals with hafted blades and grinding wild grains work together in food preparation at Ohalo II?
links.scope: Possible association between hafted cereal cutting and wild-grain processing at Ohalo II
links.finding: The blades show wear consistent with cutting near-ripe cereals, while most recovered grains show signs of full ripeness. The harvested batches and their uses cannot be matched securely.

evidence.locator: Discussion, paragraphs beginning ‘The use-wear analysis’ and ‘Large quantities’
evidence.supports: Distinct blade wear supports cereal cutting with some hafted tools. The authors note that most grains recovered at the site were ripe.
The distribution of wild grain around the grinding stone documents a separate line of evidence for cereal gathering and processing.
